program.name: freeway-single-lane-lookup-v1
program.guidance: Follow this two-step lookup rule using current positions only. Step 1: read p=observation.player[1] and select exactly ONE lane by this table: p=37..52 -> lane 0; 53..68 -> lane 1; 69..84 -> lane 2; 85..100 -> lane 3; 101..116 -> lane 4; 117..132 -> lane 5; 133..148 -> lane 6; 149..164 -> lane 7; 165..180 -> lane 8; 181..196 -> lane 9. All ranges include both ends. If p is outside 37..196 choose UP. Step 2: find the car with exactly that lane ID in observation.cars. Read only this selected car bbox[0], called x. If 35<=x<=51 choose NOOP. If x<=34 or x>=52 choose UP. Ignore every other car, even if its x is close to 44. Example: p=185 selects lane 9. If lane 9 x=8, choose UP even if another lane x=46. p=139 selects lane 6. If lane 6 x=48 choose NOOP. Never choose DOWN. This is the same reactive entry rule expressed as a lane lookup; do not predict motion, use history, or stop for an unselected lane.

action_criteria.NOOP: The ONE lane selected by player y has car x between 35 and 51 inclusive. Other lanes do not count.
action_criteria.UP: Player y outside 37..196 OR the ONE selected lane has car x<=34 or x>=52. Cars in other lanes cannot veto UP.
action_criteria.DOWN: No case in this rule selects DOWN.

author: interactive-coordinator
rationale: Round 6 reactive own-rule probe hit 10/13 waiting cases but only 13/27 advance cases, suggesting possible lane-condition binding errors. Test equivalent current-position rule with an explicit player-y-to-single-lane lookup. This is a hypothesis, not an established error cause.
